purpose: Measured, falsifiable provider capability data. DATA ONLY: no adapter, no interface, no transport. This file records what was observed on this machine so a later round can tell when a second real endpoint appears.
why_data_not_code: An interface designed against a single implementation encodes that implementation's assumptions. Only one local endpoint exists today, so an abstraction would have exactly one instance to generalise from and would need breaking when the second arrives. Recording facts is cheap and reversible; shipping an interface is neither.
method: Each row is the provider's own --help output on this machine. No network calls, no adapter executed, nothing installed.

spec.name: Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
spec.transport: JSON-RPC over stdio with LSP-style Content-Length framing
spec.canonical_repository_note: GitHub redirects the older zed-industries/agent-client-protocol path; full_name is the canonical answer. A survey citation using the old slug was corrected after the redirect was measured.

providers.help_text_observed: Start as Agent Client Protocol server

providers.implication: ACP reaches Claude Code only through a separate adapter binary, so an ACP-only plan would cover some peers and not others.
Unknown is recorded as null, never as false. An unmeasured capability must not read as an absent one.

revisit_trigger: A second provider with a measured, executable ACP endpoint. Until then any adapter interface would have one instance to generalise from.
forbidden_now: an adapter interface or transport seam
any claim that Copilot and Claude Code interoperate over ACP on this machine
relationship_to_cmux: cmux remains the runtime and the default transport. ACP would be an additional seam behind the existing interface, never a replacement.
